The ordinal sum of two antichains is a canonical non-tree poset family for Lipschitz polytopes, and its entire Euclidean-coordinate inertia—not merely volume or a contact ellipsoid—is a natural geometric invariant. The result determines exact all-size covariance and reveals distinct mechanisms for persistent common translation (uniform component) and Gaussian inter-level gap with parameter-free variance. The cube-limit affine isotropic constant coexisting with linear condition-number divergence is a motivated, nontrivial shape phenomenon; this explicit contrast is not a routine consequence of prior central symmetry or lattice-volume combinatorics. No general-poset result or downstream application is needed to make the exact structural classification worthwhile.
